items.note: Temporal-landscape frame; variant of 'in today's fast-paced world' (already banned) not yet explicitly listed
items.example: In today's rapidly evolving landscape, businesses must adapt quickly.

items.note: Universal-gravity opener; sets up false urgency; 107x AI overuse confirmed
items.example: In a world where attention is scarce, your message must land fast.

items.note: Temporal-context framing; 11x overuse; near-identical to banned variants but distinct phrasing
items.example: In an era where data drives decisions, intuition alone is not enough.

items.note: Formal variant of 'in an era where'; adds bureaucratic padding without content
items.example: In an era characterized by rapid change, resilience is essential.

items.text: as the world continues to evolve
items.note: Temporal filler; commits to no specific change; generic AI throat-clear
items.example: As the world continues to evolve, so too must our approach to leadership.

items.note: Places reader and writer in false collaborative journey; almost never literal; 16x overuse in AI text
items.example: As we navigate these challenges, clarity becomes our greatest asset.

items.note: Collaborative-exploration frame without actual exploration; AI tutorial opener
items.example: As we explore the nuances of this topic, several themes emerge.

items.note: Same collaborative-journey opener pattern; announces examination instead of doing it
items.example: As we examine the evidence, a clear pattern begins to take shape.

items.text: as we look to the future
items.note: Generic forward-looking opener; commits to no specific future claim
items.example: As we look to the future, innovation will be the key differentiator.

items.note: Contextual-era framing that often precedes nothing specific; AI uses to sound historically aware
items.example: With the advent of artificial intelligence, the rules of the game have changed.

items.note: Positional superlative opener; implies leadership without evidence; AI uses as preamble
items.example: At the forefront of this movement are a handful of visionary companies.

items.note: Scene-setting hook template; fakes depth through hypothetical framing; near-absent in human writing
items.example: Imagine a world where every student has access to personalized learning.

items.note: Scene-set hook; moderately used by human writers in storytelling contexts but AI deploys mechanically
items.example: Picture this: you walk into a meeting and everyone already knows the answer.

items.note: Generic curiosity hook; engagement-bait at section openings; stacked with obvious implied answer
items.example: Have you ever wondered why some teams consistently outperform others?

items.note: Temporal intensifier with no referent; adds urgency without evidence; confirmed cross-source AI phrase
items.example: Now more than ever, trust is the currency of leadership.

items.note: Variant of 'now more than ever'; same empty escalation pattern
items.example: More than ever before, companies are investing in employee well-being.

items.note: Manufactured-consensus opener; asserts shared knowledge to avoid justifying a claim
items.example: It's no secret that the industry is undergoing massive disruption.

items.note: Candor-performance opener; implies the reader has been avoiding a truth; AI uses as pseudo-frank hook
items.example: Let's face it, most performance reviews are a waste of time.

items.note: Same candor-performance pattern; Bloomberry names it a distinct cadence hook; implies prior dishonesty
items.example: Let's be honest, nobody reads the full report.

items.note: Manufactured-revelation opener; Bloomberry 'candor opener' pattern; implies hidden truth without revealing one
items.example: The truth is, most startups fail not from lack of ideas but from lack of execution.

items.note: Variant of 'the truth is'; emphatic candor performance without epistemic grounding
items.example: Here's the truth: shortcuts almost always cost more in the long run.

items.note: Authority-assertion opener that claims a privileged view of reality; AI uses as transition to restate points
items.example: The reality is that most organizations are not prepared for this shift.

items.note: Asserts factual grounding without providing a citation or evidence; near-identical pattern to 'the truth is'
items.example: The fact is, most people underestimate how long change takes.

items.note: Reduction opener that frames a complex issue as having a single key; AI uses to appear insightful
items.example: The key is consistency, not intensity.

items.note: Emphatic-certainty opener borrowed from political speech; AI uses to add false gravitas
items.example: Make no mistake, this decision will define the company for years.

items.note: Urgency-imperative opener; implies a deadline without specifying one; cross-source AI phrase
items.example: It's time to rethink how we approach talent development.

items.note: Formal variant of 'it's time to'; same urgency-without-deadline pattern
items.example: It is time to confront the underlying assumptions of our strategy.

items.note: If it goes without saying, AI should not say it; 14x overuse confirmed; renders the following claim trivial
items.example: It goes without saying that customer experience is critical.

items.note: Same pattern as 'it goes without saying'; negates the point of saying anything while still saying it
items.example: Needless to say, the results exceeded expectations.

items.note: Signals the writer is withholding but then states the point anyway; empty hedging opener
items.example: Suffice it to say, the rollout did not go as planned.

items.note: Meta-commentary suggesting the reader has not already considered it; epistemic preamble without evidence
items.example: It is worth considering that remote work affects different roles differently.

items.note: Bureaucratic signpost variant; 31x overuse in AI text; passive voice avoids committing to who is noting
items.example: It should be noted that this approach has significant limitations.

items.note: Throat-clearing preamble; announces the mention before making it; signals AI padding
items.example: It bears mentioning that earlier attempts at this had mixed results.

items.note: False-perspective hedge; AI uses to simulate debate without committing to a view; 15x overuse
items.example: One might argue that the benefits outweigh the costs.

items.note: Vague-attribution opener; the unnamed 'some' holds the claim at arm's length
items.example: Some might say that the pace of change is overstated.

items.note: Performed-nuance opener that avoids giving any specific answer; near-absent in human writing
items.example: There is no one-size-fits-all solution to organizational transformation.

items.note: Pre-emptive caveat that softens the following claim without adding precision; AI medical and advisory content overuses it
items.example: Generally speaking, teams with clear goals tend to outperform those without.

items.note: 7x AI overuse; backward-referencing signpost that adds no new content; variant of 'therefore' but vaguer
items.example: In light of this, a revised approach seems warranted.

items.note: 7x AI overuse; pivot phrase that announces a transition without specifying what changed
items.example: With that in mind, let us turn to the implementation phase.

items.note: 8x AI overuse; adversative pivot that follows a concession with no real contrast; already in boilerplate-framing as a prefix but not as a standalone opener target
items.example: That being said, the results were still encouraging.

items.note: Conclusion-opener that implies comprehensive weighing without showing any; AI uses as a lazy summary frame
items.example: All things considered, the project was a qualified success.

items.text: at the end of the day
items.note: 12x AI overuse; fake-wisdom distillation opener; already in prohibited-phrases but important as a sentence-initial opener signal too
items.example: At the end of the day, what matters is whether the customer is satisfied.

items.text: when all is said and done
items.note: Variant of 'at the end of the day'; in boilerplate-framing FILLER_OPENERS list but worth capturing as an opener signal
items.example: When all is said and done, trust is the foundation of every relationship.

items.text: in the grand scheme of things
items.note: Scope-inflating opener; minimizes specifics by zooming out to an unspecified grand scale
items.example: In the grand scheme of things, this setback is a minor detour.

items.note: Academic-sounding conclusion marker that follows no actual analysis; AI uses as section ender or opener
items.example: In the final analysis, the data supports a cautious approach.

items.note: Simplification-signal opener; announces clarity without achieving it; AI uses before restatements
items.example: To put it simply, the old model no longer works.

items.note: Restatement-signal opener; announces paraphrase of a point already made; padding in disguise
items.example: To put it another way, the cost of inaction exceeds the cost of change.

items.note: Redundant restatement opener; Bloomberry transition/filler list; AI uses to pad by repeating the prior sentence
items.example: In other words, speed without direction is just movement.

items.note: Causal connector used without clear antecedent; in generic-signposting TRANSITION_PATTERNS; including here for the opener-specific signal
items.example: As such, a more nuanced approach is required.

items.note: Corporate-transition opener; commits to no specific direction; 13x corporate-speak overuse; also a closer pattern
items.example: Moving forward, the team will focus on scalability.

items.note: Synonym of 'moving forward'; same empty temporal-direction opener
items.example: Going forward, all decisions will require cross-functional sign-off.

items.note: Very common in human writing as a legitimate adversative pivot; FP risk is high in isolation; signal only in high density or combined with other tells
items.example: That said, there are valid concerns about the timeline.

items.note: Pivot phrase signaling a long preamble finally ending; near-absent outside AI and listicles; cross-source confirmation
items.example: Without further ado, here are the five principles that define great leadership.

items.note: Presumptuous observer-frame opener that speaks for the reader; AI uses to signal transitions without doing the analytic work
items.example: As we can see, the trend has been consistent over the past decade.

items.note: Backward-referencing circular opener; implies prior content proved something; 'as we've explored' in ai-detection-features but this variant not yet in rules
items.example: As we've seen, each of these factors plays a crucial role.

items.note: 18x AI overuse; asserts emphasis without explaining what makes it especially true
items.example: This is particularly true for organizations that operate across multiple jurisdictions.

items.note: Mechanical consequence-signpost; AI uses multiple times per page to announce logical steps instead of writing them
items.example: This means that teams need to adapt their communication strategies accordingly.

items.note: Common in human instructional writing; slop signal only in the sub-form 'this is where it gets interesting' or similar inflation; high FP on its own
items.example: This is where the real challenge begins.

items.note: Self-labeling drama announcement; AI announces interest rather than earning it; Bloomberry documents this as a hook pattern
items.example: Here's where it gets interesting: the very solution created a new problem.

items.note: In boilerplate-framing FILLER_OPENERS; included here as a canonical opener-signpost; Bloomberry names it as one of 17 hook patterns
items.example: Here's the thing about innovation: it requires tolerance for failure.

items.note: Self-labeling significance announcement; human writers embed importance; AI announces it
items.example: This is the important part: without trust, none of the rest matters.

items.note: Hyperbolic-scope opener; AI applies to incremental developments; near-absent in careful human prose
items.example: This changes everything we thought we knew about customer behavior.

items.note: Pseudo-profound inflection-point opener; Bloomberry and ai-detection-features both flag it; near-formulaic in AI-generated speeches and articles
items.example: We stand at a crossroads, and the decisions we make today will shape tomorrow.

items.text: we are at an inflection point
items.note: Variant of crossroads/pivotal-moment framing; same empty escalation without specifying what inflects
items.example: We are at an inflection point where the old playbook no longer applies.

items.text: the stakes have never been higher
items.note: Empty escalation opener; claims maximal urgency with no comparative basis; cross-source AI confirmation
items.example: The stakes have never been higher for organizations committed to sustainability.

items.note: Performed-complexity opener that precedes no real analysis; AI uses to seem thoughtful without engaging
items.example: There are no easy answers when it comes to ethical AI governance.

items.note: False-modesty hedge opener; presents contested claims as neutral and reasonable without justification
items.example: It's fair to say that the field has evolved considerably in recent years.

items.note: Same pattern as 'it's fair to say'; claims consensus as a hedge against making a direct claim
items.example: It's safe to say that remote work is here to stay.

items.note: Sentence-initial assertion of certainty that substitutes for evidence; intensifier adverb at sentence start; not yet in significance-density markers
items.example: Undeniably, the pandemic reshaped how we think about work.

items.note: Same pattern as 'undeniably'; forecloses the question it should answer; AI uses to project confidence
items.example: Unquestionably, this represents a turning point for the industry.

items.note: Asserts certainty without evidence; confirmed in ai-detection-features; not yet in significance-density markers list
items.example: Undoubtedly, the competitive landscape will continue to shift.

items.note: Very common in human writing; slop signal only at sentence-initial position in dense clusters; FP risk is high individually but meaningful in density; Wikipedia MOS:WTW flags it
items.example: Clearly, a different approach is needed here.

items.note: Sycophantic agreement opener; implies the reader already knew something to avoid justifying it; FP risk high individually; signal in density
items.example: Of course, not every organization will face the same challenges.

items.note: Certainty-assertion opener; Wikipedia MOS:WTW editorializing list; commits to a claim without evidence
items.example: Without a doubt, leadership is the most important factor in organizational success.

items.note: Distillation-signal opener that announces a summary without providing one; ai-detection-features flags it as a conclusion opener
items.example: In essence, the problem comes down to a lack of alignment.

items.note: False-depth framing; 'at its core, X is about Y' template confirmed in ai-detection-features; announces depth without achieving it
items.example: At its core, this is a question about values, not strategy.

items.note: Sentence-initial depth-signal adverb; Blake Stockton red flag list; AI uses to inflate the importance of routine observations
items.example: Fundamentally, this is a problem of incentive misalignment.

items.note: Extremely common filler hedge; high FP individually; signal only at sentence-initial position in density; Wikipedia MOS:WTW editorializing list
items.example: Essentially, the two approaches produce the same result.
